topologies.label: Single region with zonal redundancy
topologies.detail: Protects against some infrastructure failures but not loss of the whole region.
topologies.normalResult: Normal traffic stays in one region; regional recovery depends on restore and rebuild procedures.
topologies.failureResult: The serving path is unavailable until infrastructure, data, and routing are restored elsewhere.

topologies.label: Warm standby region
topologies.detail: A smaller recovery stack receives replicated data and scales after promotion.
topologies.normalResult: The standby costs less than a full duplicate, but promotion and scale-up remain on the recovery path.
topologies.failureResult: The standby can accept reduced traffic while capacity scales; load shedding is required above the modeled 50%.

topologies.label: Two active regions with N+1 headroom
topologies.detail: Each region is provisioned to carry the full target after its peer fails.
topologies.normalResult: Both regions serve traffic and continuously exercise routing, but write ownership and consistency are more complex.
topologies.failureResult: The survivor has modeled headroom for the full target if routing, dependencies, and data convergence work as tested.
